subject: Coffee & Tea
title: The Decline of London Coffeehouses
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Decline of London Coffeehouses usable.

hook.text: By the mid-1700s, London's coffeehouses were disappearing. Tea had conquered Britain, and private clubs took over.

buildup.text: Wealthy patrons moved to exclusive gentlemen's clubs—like White's and Boodle's—leaving coffeehouses to the masses.

discovery.text: Tea imports from China skyrocketed. By 1750, Britons drank more tea than coffee—a shift that never reversed.

twist.text: The East India Company lobbied for tea because it controlled Asian trade routes. Commerce shaped a nation's taste.

climax.text: London's vibrant coffeehouse culture faded in a few decades. The institutions it birthed—Lloyd's, the Stock Exchange—lived on.

punchline.text: The coffeehouses died. But everything they created still stands.

quiz.question: Why did London coffeehouses decline in the 1700s?
options: Tea replaced coffee, and wealthy patrons moved to private clubs
